title.zh: 新唐書卷七十 表第十上 宗室世系上

meta.sourceNote: Body replaced from Wikisource raw text after ChineseNotes scrape due to glyph/encoding artifacts.

sentences.zh: 昔者周有天下，封國七十，而同姓居五十三焉，後世不以為私也，蓋所以隆本支，崇屏衞。

translations.literal: In antiquity Zhou possessed All-under-Heaven, enfeoffed seventy states, and those of the same surname numbered fifty-three; later generations did not regard this as selfishness—rather it was to elevate the root branches and honor the protective screens.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times, when the Zhou held the realm, they enfeoffed seventy states, fifty-three of them bearing the royal surname. Later ages did not see this as mere favoritism; it was meant to exalt the trunk line and strengthen the shielding branches.

sentences.zh: 雖其弊也，以侵凌王室，有末大之患，然亦崇奬扶持，猶四百餘年而後亡，蓋其德與力皆不足矣，而其勢或然也。

translations.literal: Although its defect was encroaching upon and oppressing the royal house, with the calamity of the branch outweighing the root, yet they were also honored, encouraged, and supported, and still did not perish until more than four hundred years later—presumably their virtue and strength were both insufficient, and their circumstances may have been so.
translations.idiomatic: The system had its flaw: the enfeoffed kin could encroach on the throne and bring the peril of branches outgrowing the trunk. Yet they were still honored and sustained, and the dynasty endured more than four centuries before collapse—perhaps because virtue and power alike were wanting, or because circumstances simply ran that course.

sentences.zh: 至漢鑒秦，務廣宗室，世其國地，不幸世絕若罪除，輒復續以存其祭祀，與為長久之計，故自三代以來，獨漢為長世。

translations.literal: When Han took Qin as its mirror, it strove to expand the imperial clan, making their fiefs hereditary; if a line unfortunately died out, once guilt was cleared it was promptly revived to preserve their sacrifices—a plan for long endurance—so since the Three Dynasties, Han alone has been long-lived.
translations.idiomatic: Learning from Qin's fall, Han worked to enlarge the imperial clan and make their domains hereditary. When a line died out, once any guilt was cleared the fief was promptly restored so sacrifices could continue—a policy aimed at longevity. Since the Three Dynasties, only Han has enjoyed such enduring rule.

sentences.zh: 唐有天下三百年，子孫蕃衍，可謂盛矣！

translations.literal: Tang held All-under-Heaven for three hundred years; its descendants multiplied—one may call this flourishing!
translations.idiomatic: Tang ruled the realm for three hundred years, and its descendants multiplied prodigiously—a flourishing house indeed!

sentences.zh: 其初皆有封爵，至其世遠親盡，則各隨其人賢愚，遂與異姓之臣雜而仕宦，至或流落於民間，甚可歎也！

translations.literal: At first all had enfeoffments and ranks; when generations grew distant and kinship ties were exhausted, each followed the worth or folly of the individual, and thus mixed with officials of other surnames in government service—even sinking to life among the common people, which is deeply lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: At first they all held titles and fiefs, but as generations passed and kinship thinned, each rose or fell on personal merit or folly. They mingled with officials of other surnames in office, and some even sank into common life—a cause for deep regret!

sentences.zh: 然其疏戚遠近，源流所來，可以考見，作宗室世系表。

translations.literal: Yet the degrees of kinship, near and far, and the sources from which they flowed can be examined and seen; therefore the Genealogical Tables of the Imperial Clan are compiled.
translations.idiomatic: Still, the degrees of kinship and the lines of descent can be traced, and so the Genealogical Tables of the Imperial Clan are presented here.

sentences.zh: 序李氏出自嬴姓。

translations.literal: Preface: The Li clan issued from the Ying surname.
translations.idiomatic: Preface: The Li clan traces its origin to the Ying surname.

sentences.zh: 帝顓頊高陽氏生大業，大業生女華，女華生皐陶，字庭堅，為堯大理。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuanxu of the Gaoyang clan begot Daye; Daye begot Nühua; Nühua begot Gao Yao, styled Tingjian, who served Yao as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuanxu of the Gaoyang line had a son Daye, whose daughter Nühua bore Gao Yao, styled Tingjian, who served Emperor Yao as Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 生益，益生恩成，歷虞、夏、商，世為大理，以官命族為理氏。

translations.literal: He begot Yi; Yi begot Encheng; through Yu, Xia, and Shang they generation after generation served as Ministers of Justice, and taking the office as their clan name they became the Li clan.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yao's line continued through Yi and Encheng. Under Yu, Xia, and Shang they held the post of Minister of Justice for generations, and the clan took the name Li ('minister of justice') from that office.

sentences.zh: 至紂之時，理徵字德靈，為翼隸中吳伯，以直道不容於紂，得罪而死。

translations.literal: At the time of Zhou, Li Zheng, styled Deling, was Earl of Zhongwu in Yizhou; because his upright conduct was not tolerated by Zhou, he offended and died.
translations.idiomatic: Under King Zhou of Shang, Li Zheng, styled Deling, was Earl of Zhongwu in Yizhou. His upright conduct won no favor with Zhou, and he was put to death for his offense.

sentences.zh: 其妻陳國契和氏與子利貞逃難於伊侯之墟，食木子得全，遂改理為李氏。

translations.literal: His wife, Lady Qihe of Chen, and his son Lizhen fled in distress to the ruins of the Marquis of Yi; eating the fruit of a tree they were preserved whole, and thus changed Li to the Li clan.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Qihe of Chen and their son Lizhen fled to the ruins of the Marquis of Yi. They survived by eating the fruit of a tree and changed the clan name from Li (minister of justice) to Li (plum tree).

sentences.zh: 利貞亦娶契和氏女，生昌祖，為陳大夫，家于苦縣。

translations.literal: Lizhen also married a daughter of the Qihe clan and begot Changzu, who became a grandee of Chen and made his home in Ku County.
translations.idiomatic: Lizhen married a daughter of the Qihe clan as well and had Changzu, who became a grandee of Chen and settled the family in Ku County.

sentences.zh: 生彤德，彤德曾孫碩宗，周康王賜采邑於苦縣。

translations.literal: He begot Tongde; Tongde's great-great-grandson Shuozong received from King Kang of Zhou a fief in Ku County.
translations.idiomatic: Changzu's line ran through Tongde to Shuozong, a great-great-grandson of Tongde, to whom King Kang of Zhou granted a fief in Ku County.

sentences.zh: 五世孫乾，字元果，為周上御史大夫，娶益壽氏女嬰敷，生耳，字伯陽，一字聃，周平王時為太史。

translations.literal: The fifth-generation descendant Qian, styled Yuanguo, was Senior Censor-in-Chief of Zhou; he married Yingfu, daughter of the Yishou clan, and begot Er, styled Boyang, also known as Dan, who in the time of King Ping of Zhou was Grand Astrologer.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations later came Qian, styled Yuanguo, Senior Censor-in-Chief of Zhou. He married Yingfu of the Yishou clan and had Er, styled Boyang, also called Dan, who served as Grand Astrologer under King Ping of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 其後有李宗，字尊祖，魏封於段，為干木大夫。

translations.literal: Later there was Li Zong, styled Zunzu, enfeoffed in Duan by Wei and made Grandee of Ganmu.
translations.idiomatic: Later in the line came Li Zong, styled Zunzu, enfeoffed at Duan by Wei and made Grandee of Ganmu.

sentences.zh: 生同，為趙大將軍。

translations.literal: He begot Tong, who became Grand General of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Tong, who became Grand General of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 生兌，為趙相。

translations.literal: He begot Dui, who became Chancellor of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Dui, who became Chancellor of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 生躋，趙陽安君。

translations.literal: He begot Ji, Lord of Yang'an in Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Ji, Lord of Yang'an in Zhao.

sentences.zh: 二子：曰雲，曰恪。

translations.literal: Two sons: named Yun and named Ke.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Yun and Ke.

sentences.zh: 恪生洪，字道弘，秦太子太傅。

translations.literal: Ke begot Hong, styled Daohong, Tutor to the Crown Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Ke's son Hong, styled Daohong, was Tutor to the Crown Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 生興族，字育神，一名汪，秦將軍。

translations.literal: He begot Xingzu, styled Yushen, also called Wang, a general of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He had Xingzu, styled Yushen, also known as Wang, a general of Qin.

sentences.zh: 生曇，字貴遠，趙柏人侯，入秦為御史大夫，葬柏人西。

translations.literal: He begot Tan, styled Guiyuan, Marquis of Bairen in Zhao; entering Qin he became Censor-in-Chief and was buried west of Bairen.
translations.idiomatic: He had Tan, styled Guiyuan, Marquis of Bairen in Zhao. After entering Qin service he became Censor-in-Chief and was buried west of Bairen.

sentences.zh: 生四子：崇、辨、昭、璣。

translations.literal: He begot four sons: Chong, Bian, Zhao, and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Chong, Bian, Zhao, and Ji.

sentences.zh: 崇為隴西房，璣為趙郡房。

translations.literal: Chong was the founder of the Longxi branch; Ji was the founder of the Zhao commandery branch.
translations.idiomatic: Chong founded the Longxi branch of the clan; Ji founded the Zhao commandery branch.

sentences.zh: 崇字伯祐，隴西守、南鄭公。

translations.literal: Chong, styled Boyou, was Administrator of Longxi and Duke of Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Chong, styled Boyou, served as Administrator of Longxi and was made Duke of Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 生二子：長曰平燕；

translations.literal: He begot two sons: the elder named Pingyan;
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: the elder, Pingyan;

sentences.zh: 次曰瑤，字內德，南郡守、狄道侯。

translations.literal: the younger named Yao, styled Neide, Administrator of Nan commandery and Marquis of Didao.
translations.idiomatic: and the younger, Yao, styled Neide, Administrator of Nan commandery and Marquis of Didao.

sentences.zh: 生信，字有成，大將軍、隴西侯。

translations.literal: He begot Xin, styled Youcheng, Grand General and Marquis of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yao's son Xin, styled Youcheng, was Grand General and Marquis of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 生超，一名伉，字仁高，漢大將軍、漁陽太守。

translations.literal: He begot Chao, also called Kang, styled Rengao, Grand General of Han and Administrator of Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: He had Chao, also called Kang, styled Rengao, a Han Grand General and Administrator of Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 生二子：長曰元曠，侍中；

translations.literal: He begot two sons: the elder named Yuankuang, Attendant-in-Ordinary;
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: the elder, Yuankuang, Attendant-in-Ordinary;

sentences.zh: 次曰仲翔，河東太守、征西將軍，討叛羌于素昌，戰沒，贈太尉，葬隴西狄道東川，因家焉。

translations.literal: the younger named Zhongxiang, Administrator of Hedong and General Who Pacifies the West; campaigning against rebellious Qiang at Suchang he died in battle; posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Commandant; buried in the eastern ravine of Didao in Longxi, and the family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: and the younger, Zhongxiang, Administrator of Hedong and General Who Pacifies the West. He campaigned against rebellious Qiang at Suchang, fell in battle, and was posthumously made Grand Commandant. He was buried in the eastern ravine of Didao in Longxi, where the family then settled.

sentences.zh: 生伯考，隴西、河東二郡太守。

translations.literal: He begot Bokao, Administrator of both Longxi and Hedong commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He had Bokao, who served as Administrator of both Longxi and Hedong.

sentences.zh: 生尚，成紀令，因居成紀。

translations.literal: He begot Shang, Magistrate of Chengji, and thus dwelt in Chengji.
translations.idiomatic: He had Shang, Magistrate of Chengji, and the family came to reside there.

sentences.zh: 弟向，范陽房始祖也。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xiang was the founder of the Fanyang branch.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xiang founded the Fanyang branch.

sentences.zh: 尚生廣，前將軍。

translations.literal: Shang begot Guang, Forward General.
translations.idiomatic: Shang's son Guang was Forward General.

sentences.zh: 二子：長曰當戶，生陵，字少卿，騎都尉；

translations.literal: Two sons: the elder named Danghu, who begot Ling, styled Shaoqing, Commandant of Cavalry;
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: the elder, Danghu, whose son Ling, styled Shaoqing, was Commandant of Cavalry;

sentences.zh: 次曰敢，字幼卿，郎中令、關內侯。

translations.literal: the younger named Gan, styled Youqing, Director of the Palace Secretariat and Marquis within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: and the younger, Gan, styled Youqing, Director of the Palace Secretariat and Marquis within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 生禹，字子通。

translations.literal: He begot Yu, styled Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: He had Yu, styled Zitong.

sentences.zh: 弟忠，頓丘房始祖也。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhong was the founder of the Dunqiu branch.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhong founded the Dunqiu branch.

sentences.zh: 禹生丞公，字丞公，河南太守。

translations.literal: Yu begot Chenggong, styled Chenggong, Administrator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's son Chenggong, styled Chenggong, was Administrator of Henan.

sentences.zh: 生先，字敬宗，蜀郡、北平太守。

translations.literal: He begot Xian, styled Jingzong, Administrator of Shu commandery and of Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: He had Xian, styled Jingzong, who served as Administrator of Shu and of Beiping.

sentences.zh: 生長宗，字伯禮，漁陽丞。

translations.literal: He begot Changzong, styled Boli, Assistant Magistrate of Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: He had Changzong, styled Boli, Assistant Magistrate of Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 生君況，字叔干，一字子期，博士、議郎、太中大夫。

translations.literal: He begot Junkuang, styled Shugan, also called Ziqi, Erudite, Gentleman Consultant, and Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He had Junkuang, styled Shugan, also known as Ziqi, who served as Erudite, Gentleman Consultant, and Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 生本，字上明，郎中、侍御史。

translations.literal: He begot Ben, styled Shangming, Gentleman-of-the-Palace and Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He had Ben, styled Shangming, Gentleman-of-the-Palace and Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 生次公，字仲君，巴郡太守、西夷校尉。

translations.literal: He begot Cigong, styled Zhongjun, Administrator of Ba commandery and Colonel of the Western Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He had Cigong, styled Zhongjun, Administrator of Ba and Colonel of the Western Yi.

sentences.zh: 弟恬，渤海房始祖也。

translations.literal: His younger brother Tian was the founder of the Bohai branch.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Tian founded the Bohai branch.

sentences.zh: 次公生軌，字文逸，魏臨淮太守、司農卿。

translations.literal: Cigong begot Gui, styled Wenyi, Administrator of Linhuai in Wei and Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Cigong's son Gui, styled Wenyi, was Administrator of Linhuai under Wei and Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 弟潛，申公房始祖也。

translations.literal: His younger brother Qian was the founder of the Duke of Shen branch.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Qian founded the Duke of Shen branch.

sentences.zh: 軌生隆，字彥緒，長安令、積弩將軍。

translations.literal: Gui begot Long, styled Yanxu, Magistrate of Chang'an and General of Stacked Crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's son Long, styled Yanxu, was Magistrate of Chang'an and General of Stacked Crossbows.

sentences.zh: 生艾，字世績，晉驍騎將軍、魏郡太守。

translations.literal: He begot Ai, styled Shiji, Valiant Cavalry General of Jin and Administrator of Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He had Ai, styled Shiji, Valiant Cavalry General under Jin and Administrator of Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 生雍，字儁熙，濟北、東莞二郡太守。

translations.literal: He begot Yong, styled Junxi, Administrator of both Jibei and Dongguan commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He had Yong, styled Junxi, who served as Administrator of Jibei and Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 生二子：長曰倫，丹楊房始祖也；

translations.literal: He begot two sons: the elder named Lun, founder of the Danyang branch;
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: the elder, Lun, who founded the Danyang branch;

sentences.zh: 次曰柔，字德遠，北地太守。

translations.literal: the younger named Rou, styled Deyuan, Administrator of Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: and the younger, Rou, styled Deyuan, Administrator of Beidi.

sentences.zh: 雍孫蓋，安邑房始祖也。

translations.literal: Yong's grandson Gai was the founder of the Anyi branch.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's grandson Gai founded the Anyi branch.

sentences.zh: 柔生弇，字季子，前涼張駿天水太守、武衞將軍、安西亭侯。

translations.literal: Rou begot Yan, styled Jizi, Administrator of Tianshui under Zhang Jun of Former Liang, General of Martial Guards, and Marquis of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: Rou's son Yan, styled Jizi, served Zhang Jun of Former Liang as Administrator of Tianshui and General of Martial Guards and was made Marquis of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 生昶，字仲堅，涼太子侍講。

translations.literal: He begot Chang, styled Zhongjian, Lecturer to the Crown Prince of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He had Chang, styled Zhongjian, Lecturer to the Crown Prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 生暠，字玄盛，西涼武昭王、興聖皇帝。

translations.literal: He begot Gao, styled Xuansheng, Martial and Illustrious King of Western Liang and Emperor Who Raised the Sage.
translations.idiomatic: He had Gao, styled Xuansheng, Martial and Illustrious King of Western Liang and posthumously honored as the Emperor Who Raised the Sage.

sentences.zh: 十子：譚、歆、讓、愔、恂、翻、豫、宏、眺、亮。

translations.literal: Ten sons: Tan, Xin, Rang, Yin, Xun, Fan, Yu, Hong, Tiao, and Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He had ten sons: Tan, Xin, Rang, Yin, Xun, Fan, Yu, Hong, Tiao, and Liang.

sentences.zh: 愔，鎮遠將軍房始祖也。

translations.literal: Yin was the founder of the General Who Pacifies the Distance branch.
translations.idiomatic: Yin founded the General Who Pacifies the Distance branch.

sentences.zh: 其曾孫系，平涼房始祖也。

translations.literal: His great-great-grandson Xi was the founder of the Pingliang branch.
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-grandson Xi founded the Pingliang branch.

sentences.zh: 翻孫三人：曰丞，姑臧房始祖也；

translations.literal: Fan's grandsons, three in number: named Cheng, founder of the Guzang branch;
translations.idiomatic: Fan had three grandsons: Cheng, who founded the Guzang branch;

sentences.zh: 曰茂，燉煌房始祖也；

translations.literal: named Mao, founder of the Dunhuang branch;
translations.idiomatic: Mao, who founded the Dunhuang branch;

sentences.zh: 曰沖，僕射房始祖也。

translations.literal: and named Chong, founder of the Vice Director branch.
translations.idiomatic: and Chong, who founded the Vice Director branch.

sentences.zh: 曾孫曰成禮，絳郡房始祖也。

translations.literal: A great-great-grandson named Chenli was the founder of the Jiang commandery branch.
translations.idiomatic: A great-great-grandson, Chenli, founded the Jiang commandery branch.

sentences.zh: 豫玄孫曰剛，武陵房始祖也。

translations.literal: Yu's great-great-grandson named Gang was the founder of the Wuling branch.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's great-great-grandson Gang founded the Wuling branch.

sentences.zh: 歆字士業，西涼後主。

translations.literal: Xin, styled Shiye, was the last ruler of Western Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Xin, styled Shiye, was the last ruler of Western Liang.

sentences.zh: 八子：勗、紹、重耳、弘之、崇明、崇產、崇庸、崇祐。

translations.literal: Eight sons: Xu, Shao, Chong'er, Hongzhi, Chongming, Chongchan, Chongyong, and Chongyou.
translations.idiomatic: He had eight sons: Xu, Shao, Chong'er, Hongzhi, Chongming, Chongchan, Chongyong, and Chongyou.

sentences.zh: 重耳字景順，以國亡奔宋，為汝南太守。

translations.literal: Chong'er, styled Jingshun, when the state perished fled to Song and became Administrator of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Chong'er, styled Jingshun, fled to Song after the kingdom fell and became Administrator of Runan.

sentences.zh: 後魏克豫州，以地歸之，拜恒農太守，復為宋將薛安都所陷，後魏安南將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Later Wei captured Yuzhou and returned the territory to him; he was appointed Administrator of Hengnong; again he was taken by Song general Xue Andu; he became General Who Pacifies the South of Later Wei and Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Wei seized Yuzhou it restored his lands and made him Administrator of Hengnong. He was later captured by the Song general Xue Andu, then served Northern Wei as General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 生獻祖宣皇帝熙，字孟良，後魏金門鎮將。

translations.literal: He begot the Founding Ancestor, Emperor Xuan, Xi, styled Mengliang, Garrison Commander of Jinmen under Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He had Xi, styled Mengliang, posthumously the Founding Ancestor Emperor Xuan, who served Later Wei as Garrison Commander of Jinmen.

sentences.zh: 生懿祖光皇帝，諱天賜，字德真。

translations.literal: He begot the Illustrious Ancestor, Emperor Guang, taboo name Tianci, styled Dezhen.
translations.idiomatic: He had Tianci, styled Dezhen, posthumously the Illustrious Ancestor Emperor Guang.

sentences.zh: 三子：長曰起頭，長安侯，生達摩，後周羽林監、太子洗馬、長安縣伯，其後無聞；

translations.literal: Three sons: the elder named Qitou, Marquis of Chang'an, who begot Damo, Supervisor of the Feathered Forest under Later Zhou, Groom of the Heir Apparent, and Baron of Chang'an county—afterward no report;
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: the elder, Qitou, Marquis of Chang'an, whose son Damo served Later Zhou as Supervisor of the Feathered Forest, Groom of the Heir Apparent, and Baron of Chang'an county—his line is not recorded further;

sentences.zh: 次曰太祖；

translations.literal: the second named the Grand Ancestor;
translations.idiomatic: the second, the Grand Ancestor;

sentences.zh: 次乞豆。

translations.literal: the third Qidou.
translations.idiomatic: and the third, Qidou.

sentences.zh: 定州刺史房

translations.literal: Branch of the Inspector of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Inspector of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 太祖太祖景皇帝虎，字文彬，後周柱國大將軍、唐國襄公。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor, Emperor Jing, Hu, styled Wenbin, Pillar-of-the-State Grand General of Later Zhou and Duke of Xiang of the State of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor, Emperor Jing, Hu, styled Wenbin, served Later Zhou as Pillar-of-the-State Grand General and was Duke of Xiang of Tang.

sentences.zh: 八子，長曰延伯，生於山東。

translations.literal: Eight sons; the eldest named Yanbo was born east of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He had eight sons; the eldest, Yanbo, was born east of the mountains.

sentences.zh: 其後太祖入關，延伯仕北齊為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Afterward the Grand Ancestor entered the passes; Yanbo served Northern Qi as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Grand Ancestor entered the passes, Yanbo remained in Northern Qi as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 武德四年，追封南陽伯，附屬籍，貞觀初，罷之，與姑臧、絳郡、武陽公三房，號「四公子」房，至開元二十三年，復附屬籍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude he was posthumously enfeoffed as Baron of Nanyang and attached to the register; at the beginning of Zhenguan this was abolished; together with the three branches of Guzang, Jiang commandery, and Duke of Wuyang they were called the 'Four Dukes' Sons' branches; by the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan they were again attached to the register.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude year 4 he was posthumously made Baron of Nanyang and enrolled in the imperial clan register. Early in Zhenguan that enrollment was revoked. Together with the Guzang, Jiang commandery, and Duke of Wuyang branches they were known as the 'Four Dukes' Sons' houses. In Kaiyuan year 23 they were enrolled again.

sentences.zh: 南陽公房

translations.literal: Branch of the Duke of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Duke of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 譙王房

translations.literal: Branch of the Prince of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Prince of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 蔡王房

translations.literal: Branch of the Prince of Cai.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Prince of Cai.

sentences.zh: 畢王房

translations.literal: Branch of the Prince of Bi.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Prince of Bi.

sentences.zh: 雍王房

translations.literal: Branch of the Prince of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Prince of Yong.

sentences.zh: 郇王房

translations.literal: Branch of the Prince of Xun.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Prince of Xun.

sentences.zh: 大鄭王房

translations.literal: Branch of the Great Prince of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Great Prince of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 代祖代祖元皇帝諱昺，周安州總管、柱國大將軍、唐國仁公。

translations.literal: The Ancestral Substitute, Emperor Yuan, taboo name Bing, General-in-Chief of Anzhou under Zhou, Pillar-of-the-State Grand General, and Duke of Ren of the State of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: The Ancestral Substitute, Emperor Yuan, Bing, served Zhou as General-in-Chief of Anzhou and Pillar-of-the-State Grand General and was Duke of Ren of Tang.

sentences.zh: 四子：長曰高祖，次曰梁王澄，次曰蜀王湛，次曰漢王洪。

translations.literal: Four sons: the eldest was the High Ancestor; the second was Prince of Liang, Cheng; the third was Prince of Shu, Zhan; the fourth was Prince of Han, Hong.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: the eldest became the High Ancestor; the second was Prince of Liang, Cheng; the third Prince of Shu, Zhan; and the fourth Prince of Han, Hong.

sentences.zh: 梁王房

translations.literal: Branch of the Prince of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 蜀王房，後為渤海王房。

translations.literal: Branch of the Prince of Shu, later the branch of the Prince of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Prince of Shu, later known as the House of the Prince of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 高祖高祖神堯大聖大光孝皇帝二十二子，分十五房：曰楚王智雲，曰荊王元景，曰徐王元禮，曰韓王元嘉，曰彭王元則，曰鄭王元懿，曰霍王元軌，曰虢王鳳，曰道王元慶，曰鄧王元裕，曰舒王元名，曰魯王靈夔，曰江王元祥，曰密王元曉，曰滕王元嬰。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor, the Divine Yao, Great Sage, Greatly Illuminated, Filial Emperor, had twenty-two sons, divided into fifteen branches: namely Prince of Chu, Zhiyun; Prince of Jing, Yuanjing; Prince of Xu, Yuanli; Prince of Han, Yuanjia; Prince of Peng, Yuanze; Prince of Zheng, Yuanyi; Prince of Huo, Yuangui; Prince of Guo, Feng; Prince of Dao, Yuanqing; Prince of Deng, Yuanyu; Prince of Shu, Yuanming; Prince of Lu, Lingkui; Prince of Jiang, Yuanxiang; Prince of Mi, Yuanxiao; and Prince of Teng, Yuanying.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor, Emperor Gaozu, had twenty-two sons grouped into fifteen houses: the Princes of Chu (Zhiyun), Jing (Yuanjing), Xu (Yuanli), Han (Yuanjia), Peng (Yuanze), Zheng (Yuanyi), Huo (Yuangui), Guo (Feng), Dao (Yuanqing), Deng (Yuanyu), Shu (Yuanming), Lu (Lingkui), Jiang (Yuanxiang), Mi (Yuanxiao), and Teng (Yuanying).

sentences.zh: 智雲、元景皆無後。

translations.literal: Zhiyun and Yuanjing both had no descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyun and Yuanjing left no descendants.

sentences.zh: 徐王房

translations.literal: Branch of the Prince of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Prince of Xu.

sentences.zh: 韓王房，建中元年詔改為嗣鄆王房，懿宗即位，復舊。

translations.literal: Branch of the Prince of Han; in the first year of Jianzhong an edict changed it to the branch of the Heir of Yan; when Emperor Yizong took the throne, the former name was restored.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Prince of Han. In the first year of Jianzhong an edict renamed it the House of the Heir of Yan; when Emperor Yizong acceded, the old name was restored.

sentences.zh: 彭王房

translations.literal: Branch of the Prince of Peng.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Prince of Peng.

sentences.zh: 小鄭王房，稱惠鄭王房。

translations.literal: Branch of the Lesser Prince of Zheng, also called the branch of the Kind Prince of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Lesser Prince of Zheng, also called the House of the Kind Prince of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 霍王房

translations.literal: Branch of the Prince of Huo.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Prince of Huo.

sentences.zh: 虢王房

translations.literal: Branch of the Prince of Guo.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Prince of Guo.

sentences.zh: 道王房

translations.literal: Branch of the Prince of Dao.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Prince of Dao.

sentences.zh: 鄧王房

translations.literal: Branch of the Prince of Deng.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Prince of Deng.

sentences.zh: 舒王房，建中元年改為嗣郢王房。

translations.literal: Branch of the Prince of Shu; in the first year of Jianzhong changed to the branch of the Heir of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Prince of Shu. In the first year of Jianzhong it was renamed the House of the Heir of Ying.

sentences.zh: 魯王房，寶應元年改為嗣鄒王房。

translations.literal: Branch of the Prince of Lu; in the first year of Baoying changed to the branch of the Heir of Zou.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Prince of Lu. In the first year of Baoying it was renamed the House of the Heir of Zou.

sentences.zh: 江王房

translations.literal: Branch of the Prince of Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Prince of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 密王房

translations.literal: Branch of the Prince of Mi.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Prince of Mi.

sentences.zh: 滕王房

translations.literal: Branch of the Prince of Teng.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Prince of Teng.

sentences.zh: 太宗太宗文武大聖大廣孝皇帝十四子：長曰恒山愍王承乾，次曰楚王寬，出繼。

translations.literal: Taizong, the Literary and Martial, Great Sage, Greatly Extensive, Filial Emperor, had fourteen sons: the eldest was the Lamented Prince of Hengshan, Chengqian; the second was Prince of Chu, Kuan, who was given in adoption.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong had fourteen sons: the eldest was the Lamented Prince of Hengshan, Chengqian; the second was Prince of Chu, Kuan, who was given in adoption to another line.

sentences.zh: 次曰吳王恪，次曰濮王泰，次曰庶人祐，附濮王譜。

translations.literal: Next Prince of Wu, Ke; next Prince of Pu, Tai; next the commoner You, attached to the genealogy of the Prince of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Prince of Wu, Ke; then Prince of Pu, Tai; then the commoner You, enrolled under the Prince of Pu's genealogy.

sentences.zh: 次曰蜀王愔，次曰蔣王惲，次曰越王貞，次曰高宗，次曰紀王慎，次曰江王嚻，次曰代王簡，次曰趙王福，次曰曹王明。

translations.literal: Next Prince of Shu, Yin; next Prince of Jiang, Yun; next Prince of Yue, Zhen; next the High Ancestor; next Prince of Ji, Shen; next Prince of Jiang, Xi; next Prince of Dai, Jian; next Prince of Zhao, Fu; next Prince of Cao, Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Then Prince of Shu, Yin; Prince of Jiang, Yun; Prince of Yue, Zhen; the future Emperor Gaozong; Prince of Ji, Shen; Prince of Jiang, Xi; Prince of Dai, Jian; Prince of Zhao, Fu; and Prince of Cao, Ming.

sentences.zh: 嚻、簡、福皆附曹王譜。

translations.literal: Xi, Jian, and Fu were all attached to the genealogy of the Prince of Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, Jian, and Fu were all enrolled under the Prince of Cao's genealogy.

sentences.zh: 恒山愍王房

translations.literal: Branch of the Lamented Prince of Hengshan.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Lamented Prince of Hengshan.

sentences.zh: 吳王房

translations.literal: Branch of the Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Prince of Wu.

translations.literal: Branch of the Prince of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Prince of Pu.

translations.idiomatic: House of the Prince of Yue.

translations.literal: Branch of the Prince of Cao.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Prince of Cao.

sentences.zh: 高宗高宗天皇大聖大弘孝皇帝八子。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor, the Heavenly Sovereign, Great Sage, Greatly Expansive, Filial Emperor, had eight sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong had eight sons.

sentences.zh: 燕王房。

translations.literal: Branch of the Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 澤王房。

translations.literal: Branch of the Prince of Ze.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Prince of Ze.

sentences.zh: 許王房。

translations.literal: Branch of the Prince of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Prince of Xu.

sentences.zh: 大邠章懷太子房。

translations.literal: Branch of the Great Crown Prince of Zhanghuai of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Great Crown Prince Zhanghuai of Bin.

sentences.zh: 中宗中宗大和大聖大昭孝皇帝四子。

translations.literal: Zhongzong, the Greatly Harmonious, Great Sage, Greatly Illuminated, Filial Emperor, had four sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong had four sons.

sentences.zh: 湖陽郡王房

translations.literal: Branch of the Prince of Huyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Prince of Huyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 睿宗睿宗玄真大聖大興孝皇帝六子。

translations.literal: Ruizong, the Mysteriously True, Great Sage, Greatly Prospering, Filial Emperor, had six sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ruizong had six sons.

sentences.zh: 讓皇帝房，亦曰寧王房

translations.literal: Branch of the Emperor Who Yielded, also called the branch of the Prince of Ning.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Emperor Who Yielded, also called the House of the Prince of Ning.

sentences.zh: 惠莊太子房，亦曰申王房。

translations.literal: Branch of the Kind and Stately Crown Prince, also called the branch of the Prince of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Kind and Stately Crown Prince, also called the House of the Prince of Shen.

sentences.zh: 惠文太子房，亦曰岐王房。

translations.literal: Branch of the Kind and Literary Crown Prince, also called the branch of the Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Kind and Literary Crown Prince, also called the House of the Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 惠宣太子房，亦曰薛王房。

translations.literal: Branch of the Kind and Illustrious Crown Prince, also called the branch of the Prince of Xue.
translations.idiomatic: House of the Kind and Illustrious Crown Prince, also called the House of the Prince of Xue.

sentences.zh: 玄宗玄宗至道大聖大明孝皇帝二十三子。

translations.literal: Xuanzong, the Utmost Way, Great Sage, Greatly Illuminated, Filial Emperor, had twenty-three sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong had twenty-three sons.

sentences.zh: 自玄宗以後，諸王不出閤，不分房，子孫闕而不見。

translations.literal: From Xuanzong onward, the princes did not leave the palace quarters, branches were not divided, and descendants were missing and not seen.
translations.idiomatic: From Xuanzong onward the princes no longer left the inner quarters, branches were no longer distinguished, and their descendants are largely unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 肅宗肅宗文明武德大聖大宣孝皇帝十四子。

translations.literal: Suzong, the Cultured and Martial, Martial and Virtuous, Great Sage, Greatly Proclaiming, Filial Emperor, had fourteen sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong had fourteen sons.

sentences.zh: 代宗代宗睿文孝武皇帝二十子。

translations.literal: Daizong, the Sagaciously Literary, Filial and Martial Emperor, had twenty sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong had twenty sons.

sentences.zh: 德宗德宗神武孝文皇帝十一子。

translations.literal: Dezong, the Divinely Martial, Filial and Literary Emperor, had eleven sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong had eleven sons.

sentences.zh: 順宗順宗至德弘道大聖大安孝皇帝二十二子。

translations.literal: Shunzong, the Utmost Virtue, Expansive Way, Great Sage, Greatly Tranquil, Filial Emperor, had twenty-two sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shunzong had twenty-two sons.

sentences.zh: 憲宗憲宗昭文章武大聖至神孝皇帝二十子。

translations.literal: Xianzong, the Illustriously Literary and Martial, Great Sage, Utmost Divine, Filial Emperor, had twenty sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong had twenty sons.

sentences.zh: 穆宗穆宗睿聖文惠孝皇帝五子。

translations.literal: Muzong, the Sagaciously Holy, Literary and Kind, Filial Emperor, had five sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong had five sons.

sentences.zh: 敬宗敬宗睿武昭愍孝皇帝五子。

translations.literal: Jingzong, the Sagaciously Martial, Illustrious and Lamenting, Filial Emperor, had five sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingzong had five sons.

sentences.zh: 文宗文宗元聖昭獻孝皇帝二子。

translations.literal: Wenzong, the Primal Sage, Illustrious and Offering, Filial Emperor, had two sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong had two sons.

sentences.zh: 武宗武宗至道昭肅孝皇帝五子。

translations.literal: Wuzong, the Utmost Way, Illustrious and Solemn, Filial Emperor, had five sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong had five sons.

sentences.zh: 宣宗宣宗元聖至明成武獻文睿知章仁神德懿道大孝皇帝十一子。

translations.literal: Xuanzong, the Primal Sage, Utmost Illuminated, Accomplished and Martial, Offering and Literary, Sagaciously Knowing, Manifestly Benevolent, Divinely Virtuous, Morally Admirable, Utmost Way, Greatly Filial Emperor, had eleven sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong had eleven sons.

sentences.zh: 懿宗懿宗昭聖恭惠孝皇帝八子。

translations.literal: Yizong, the Illustriously Holy, Respectful and Kind, Filial Emperor, had eight sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yizong had eight sons.

sentences.zh: 僖宗僖宗聖神聰睿仁哲明孝皇帝二子。

translations.literal: Xizong, the Sagely Divine, Cleverly Sagacious, Benevolent and Wise, Illuminated and Filial Emperor, had two sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong had two sons.

sentences.zh: 昭宗昭宗聖文睿德光武弘孝皇帝十七子。

translations.literal: Zhaozong, the Sagely Literary, Sagaciously Virtuous, Illuminated and Martial, Expansive and Filial Emperor, had seventeen sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong had seventeen sons.

sentences.zh: 【結】宗室四十一房：一曰定州刺史，二曰南陽公，三曰譙王，四曰蔡王，五曰畢王，六曰雍王，七曰郇王，八曰大鄭王，九曰蜀王，十曰巢王，十一曰大楚王，十二曰荊王，十三曰徐王，十四曰韓王，十五曰彭王，十六曰小鄭王，十七曰霍王，十八曰虢王，十九曰道王，二十曰鄧王，二十一曰舒王，二十二曰魯王，二十三曰江王，二十四曰密王，二十五曰滕王，二十六曰恒山王，二十七曰吳王，二十八曰濮王，二十九曰蔣王，三十曰越王，三十一曰紀王，三十二曰曹王，三十三曰澤王，三十四曰章懷太子，三十五曰湖陽郡王，三十六曰讓皇帝，三十七曰惠莊太子，三十八曰惠文太子，三十九曰惠宣太子，蜀王房又有隴西、渤海二房附見其譜，定著三十九房。

translations.literal: [Conclusion] The imperial clan had forty-one branches: first the Inspector of Dingzhou; second the Duke of Nanyang; third the Prince of Qiao; fourth the Prince of Cai; fifth the Prince of Bi; sixth the Prince of Yong; seventh the Prince of Xun; eighth the Great Prince of Zheng; ninth the Prince of Shu; tenth the Prince of Chao; eleventh the Great Prince of Chu; twelfth the Prince of Jing; thirteenth the Prince of Xu; fourteenth the Prince of Han; fifteenth the Prince of Peng; sixteenth the Lesser Prince of Zheng; seventeenth the Prince of Huo; eighteenth the Prince of Guo; nineteenth the Prince of Dao; twentieth the Prince of Deng; twenty-first the Prince of Shu; twenty-second the Prince of Lu; twenty-third the Prince of Jiang; twenty-fourth the Prince of Mi; twenty-fifth the Prince of Teng; twenty-sixth the Prince of Hengshan; twenty-seventh the Prince of Wu; twenty-eighth the Prince of Pu; twenty-ninth the Prince of Jiang; thirtieth the Prince of Yue; thirty-first the Prince of Ji; thirty-second the Prince of Cao; thirty-third the Prince of Ze; thirty-fourth the Crown Prince Zhanghuai; thirty-fifth the Prince of Huyang commandery; thirty-sixth the Emperor Who Yielded; thirty-seventh the Kind and Stately Crown Prince; thirty-eighth the Kind and Literary Crown Prince; thirty-ninth the Kind and Illustrious Crown Prince—the branch of the Prince of Shu also had the Longxi and Bohai branches attached and seen in its genealogy; definitively recorded are thirty-nine branches.
translations.idiomatic: [Conclusion] The imperial clan comprised forty-one named houses: the Inspector of Dingzhou; the Duke of Nanyang; the Princes of Qiao, Cai, Bi, Yong, Xun, Zheng (Great), Shu, Chao, Chu (Great), Jing, Xu, Han, Peng, Zheng (Lesser), Huo, Guo, Dao, Deng, Shu, Lu, Jiang, Mi, Teng, Hengshan, Wu, Pu, Jiang, Yue, Ji, Cao, Ze, Crown Prince Zhanghuai, Prince of Huyang, the Emperor Who Yielded, and the Kind and Stately, Kind and Literary, and Kind and Illustrious Crown Princes. The House of the Prince of Shu also includes the Longxi and Bohai branches in its genealogy. Thirty-nine houses are definitively recorded.

sentences.zh: 終唐之世，有宰相十一人。

translations.literal: Throughout the Tang dynasty there were eleven men who served as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Tang dynasty, eleven members of the imperial clan served as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 郇王房有林甫、回；

translations.literal: The branch of the Prince of Xun had Linpu and Hui;
translations.idiomatic: The House of the Prince of Xun produced Linpu and Hui;

sentences.zh: 鄭王房有程、石、福；

translations.literal: the branch of the Prince of Zheng had Cheng, Shi, and Fu;
translations.idiomatic: the House of the Prince of Zheng produced Cheng, Shi, and Fu;

sentences.zh: 小鄭王房有勉、夷簡、宗閔；

translations.literal: the branch of the Lesser Prince of Zheng had Mian, Yijian, and Zongmin;
translations.idiomatic: the House of the Lesser Prince of Zheng produced Mian, Yijian, and Zongmin;

sentences.zh: 恒山王房有適之；

translations.literal: the branch of the Prince of Hengshan had Shizhi;
translations.idiomatic: the House of the Prince of Hengshan produced Shizhi;

sentences.zh: 吳王房有峴；

translations.literal: the branch of the Prince of Wu had Xian;
translations.idiomatic: the House of the Prince of Wu produced Xian;

sentences.zh: 惠宣太子房有知柔。

translations.literal: the branch of the Kind and Illustrious Crown Prince had Zhirou.
translations.idiomatic: and the House of the Kind and Illustrious Crown Prince produced Zhirou.
